name: – Konstantinos Arvanitis – § 44 – Am 16
title: REPORT on the Commission’s 2025 Rule of Law report
part_text: 44. Calls on the Member States, candidate countries and potential candidate countries, as well as EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies, to establish or strengthen preventive measures against corruption, such as specialised and independent anti-corruption institutions, transparent management of EU funds, strengthened or proper enforcement of transparency requirements in decision-making, such as registers of lobbyists and reporting obligations on political funding, ensuring a high level of transparency in the relevant EU policy areas, codes of conduct for public officials, mandatory asset declarations and verification thereof, early warning systems, and clear rules on conflict-of-interest and revolving-door practices; stresses that the deliberate failure by any high-level public official to comply with these obligations, in particular the Minister for Justice of a Member State, is unacceptable, and therefore condemns a situation where, instead of fully disclosing substantial assets and dispelling all doubts as to their origin, a high-level public official has chosen to attack public officials and journalists who have raised this matter, thereby failing to set an example of integrity and instead contributing to a climate of opacity and the erosion of anti-corruption rules;
